newsitem.title: USA: Clinton urges NATO buy U.S. J-Star planes.
newsitem.headline: Clinton urges NATO buy U.S. J-Star planes.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Thursday he would urge NATO to purchase Northrop Grumman's J-Star surveillance aircraft in what could turn into a contract battle with France, Britain and Italy.

Noting that NATO's military committee earlier in Brussels had agreed that an air surveillance system was needed, Clinton told a crowd at Northrop Grumman's hangar in Lake Charles, Louisiana: "Now it's my job to tell them what air surveillance system we need -- the J-Stars -- and I'll do my best."

NATO defense ministers will consider the issue further in December. The United States believes 300 jobs could be added to the payroll at Northrop Grumman's production facility in Lake Charles if NATO buys 10 and would carry production through 2007.

Known as the Joint Surveillance Target Attack Radar System (J-Stars), the planes are Boeing 707s fitted with a powerful surveillance and target acquisition radar system to distinguish moving or fixed targets from other types of objects on the ground.
France, Britain and Italy are pushing competing designs. Britain has the as-yet unbuilt Astor, France the Horizon and Italy the Creso.
The United States has offered NATO bids of five, 10 or 15 aircraft. The Defense Department agreed to buy 19 for the U.S. Air Force at a cost of about $9 billion.
